observation_summary: The resetMock method in MockUtil was failing to preserve invocation listeners when a mock was reset, causing subsequent verifications to fail.
reasoning_summary: The fix involves changing how the new mock handler is initialized during a reset. Instead of creating a new handler with default settings, the fix retrieves the existing mock settings from the old handler and uses them to create the new filter. This ensures that the association between the mock and its configured listeners is maintained across the reset operation. This is a classic relationship/consistency issue between the state of the old mock and the new mock state after reset.
evidence_used: The fix_diff_oracle shows that resetMock was changed from creating a new MockHandler with default settings to using newMethodInterceptorFilter(oldMockHandler.getMockSettings()).
The failing test indicates that invocation listeners were lost after a reset operation.

alternative_types.why_not_primary: While the fix involves changing how the new filter is initialized, the root cause is the failure to maintain the relationship/association between the existing mock configuration (listeners) and the reset mock state.
The fix is not about the internal logic of a computation, but about ensuring the structural consistency of the mock object's configuration after a reset.
